titleSource: System Reset: Being Unreasonable and Unambiguous

sittings.bodyEn: A class was offered a trip anywhere if they contacted three seemingly unreachable people and got one of them to answer three questions. The first group, about twenty students, finished zero, mostly because each one assumed the others would do it better. A later group that heard that result finished six of seventeen attempts in under forty-eight hours. Even a messy one-paragraph reply would have won the first year, by the rules that were set. Realistic goals draw the thickest competition, which makes them slower than they look. An unusually large goal is easier to sustain because it supplies endurance for the messy middle, and the chapter claims that raising one million dollars can be easier than raising one hundred thousand. Big aims also face less competition, because most people aim at the crowded middle.

terms.hook: A target large enough to supply endurance, in a lane with less competition.

sittings.bodyEn: What do you want is too vague to produce an action, and so is a bare question about your goals. The useful question is what would excite you. Happiness, in this chapter, is too blurry and too easy to fake with a bottle of wine. The opposite of happiness here is boredom, and excitement is the practical stand-in you are told to chase. When work is removed and you have not named the activities that replace it, the dollar target inflates forever so you never have to face the empty week. That is how employees and owners become the tired person in the expensive car, fifteen or twenty years along the same track. Boredom is the enemy, and a friend is allowed to ask whether you are turning into that person whenever your aims shrink.

terms.hook: The practical stand-in for happiness, and the feeling the goals are supposed to create.
The slide, after school, into a realistic life with no scheduled adventure.

sittings.bodyEn: Dreamlining puts timelines on aims most people would file under dreams. It differs from ordinary goal-setting in three ways. A fuzzy wish has to become a step you can do. The aim has to be too large for the usual crowd, or the sheet will not pull you through trouble. The sheet also names the activities that will fill the week once extra work is gone, because a rich life here is a string of experiences, with objects only as tools. Use it when the tired future reappears, and expect it to be hard in proportion to how much you need it. The steps below are the whole method, in order.

terms.hook: Timelines plus defined steps for unrealistic aims, including the life that replaces excess work.

sittings.bodyEn: Make a six-month list and a twelve-month list. On each, write up to five things for having, up to five for being, and up to five for doing, in that order. Having can include a house, a car, or clothes, and it is not limited to objects. Being might be a great cook or fluent in a language, and doing might be a place, a trip to your roots, or a strange race. If a box is empty, write the opposite of what you hate or fear in that column. Leave the list large, and ignore the method until a later step. Keep a real want even when it is ordinary or a little vain, and do not replace a true want with a virtuous one out of guilt.

The doing column is where most people go blank, even when they can complain in detail about what blocks them. Ask what you would do, day to day, with one hundred million dollars in the bank. Ask what would make you excited to wake up tomorrow. Give those two questions a few minutes before you declare the column empty. If you are still stuck, fill the five doing spots with a set list. Use a place you want to see, a memory you want before the end, a daily act, a weekly act, and a skill you have always meant to learn. That set is a starter, not a ceiling.

Convert every being into a doing, because being is only a holding spot for an action. Name an action that would show the state, or a finished job that would prove it is real. A great cook becomes making a holiday dinner without help. Fluent in a language becomes a five-minute conversation with a coworker who speaks it. People find being easier to brainstorm, which is why it comes second on the sheet. Leave no being that cannot be pointed at a visible act. The later steps only price and schedule doings.

On the six-month sheet, star the four dreams, from any column, that would change the most or excite you most. Repeat that starring on the twelve-month sheet if you want a second pass. Turn each of the four into a monthly cost, and spread a one-time price across the months in the timeline, as the chapter's reader note corrects the sheet. Some of those monthly figures can be zero. Add your ordinary monthly living cost, then add another thirty percent of that living cost as a buffer for safety or savings. Dream costs plus that buffered living cost are your target monthly income. Divide that monthly target by thirty to get a target daily income, which is the number to carry into the rest of the book.

terms.hook: The monthly dream costs plus living costs with a thirty percent buffer.
The monthly target divided by thirty.

sittings.bodyEn: Prefer three-month and six-month lines, because a far-off plan becomes permission to wait. For each of the four six-month dreams, write three steps: one for now, one for tomorrow before eleven in the morning, and one for the day after, again before eleven. Do not outline every step from here to the end. The aim is the end state, the income number that funds it, and momentum. Do the three now actions immediately, and shrink any one of them until it takes about five minutes. If it is the middle of the night and the step is a call, send a message now and dial as soon as the morning starts. If the next stage is research, ask someone who has done the thing, because more reading easily becomes a stall, and you can also book a class you would feel bad canceling.

The chapter measures success by how many uncomfortable conversations you will have. The contact shape is a personal email when you can find one, often through a little-known site they actually write. Use two or three paragraphs that show you know the work, then one question that is easy to answer and still worth their time. The question should touch their work or how they see a life, and the goal of the first note is a dialogue. A request for help waits until three or four genuine exchanges have happened. One student in the chapter kept asking a single gatekeeper, including a third time, instead of spraying messages at random. Either persistence or a wider net can get a reply, and the point of the contest is that the realistic silence was optional.

From this chapter on, the book adds one comfort challenge at a time, usually for two days, marked on a calendar so you do not stack them. The link it claims is direct: a wider comfort zone and getting what you want move together. This chapter's challenge is eye gaze. For two days, hold one person's eyes, someone you pass or someone you are talking with, until they look away. Focus on one eye, blink so you do not freeze into a stare, and keep the contact while you are the one speaking, which is the harder moment. Practice with people who seem bigger or more confident than you. If someone asks why you are looking, smile and say you thought they were an old friend.

Dreamlining starts with unrealistic having, being, and doing on a six-month sheet and a twelve-month sheet. Beings become doings, four dreams are starred, and their monthly cost plus buffered living costs becomes the income target. A one-time price is spread across the months so it does not pretend to be a permanent bill. The first actions are tiny, immediate, and aimed at a person who has done the thing when the step would otherwise be more reading. Excitement is the test of a goal, because a realistic aim often dies at the first obstacle. The unreachable note is a short, informed question whose job is a conversation, with any favor waiting until trust exists.
choices: Pick a realistic salary, buy the tools, and schedule the life after you retire
List having, being, and doing, turn beings into doings, price four dreams into a monthly target, and do a five-minute step now
Read until the method feels complete, then contact someone famous to ask for a job
Set a five-year plan with every step mapped, and wait for a free weekend to begin
